name: United States Senate Youth Program (USSYP)
value: $12,500 college scholarship for each delegate, plus an all-expenses-paid Washington Week (March 6 to 13, 2027)
deadline: State selection deadlines vary; states must submit their delegate selections by December 1, 2026
apply: Contact your state selection contact (listed on the USSYP site) for your state's application and deadline.
eligibility: Outstanding high school students interested in public service who are actively serving in high-level elected or appointed leadership positions. Two delegates are chosen per state, DC, and DoDEA.
notes: Your state's own deadline is earlier than the December 1 national deadline. Some states list their application as on hold until posted.

name: National High School Oratorical Contest
value: National winner $25,000; second $22,500; third $20,000; each state winner in the national first round $2,000, plus $2,000 more for advancing past round one. Over $203,500 total.
deadline: Starts at the local post level; post and department (state) contest dates are set locally
apply: Contact a local American Legion post or your state department to enter. Prepare an 8 to 10 minute oration on the Constitution plus an assigned-topic discourse (2027 topics are posted).
eligibility: Students under age 20 enrolled in high school (grades 9 to 12, public, private, parochial, military or home school) who are U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents.
notes: Scholarships may be used at any U.S. college or university.

provider: National Society Daughters of the American Revolution
name: DAR Good Citizens Award and Scholarship Contest
value: Scholarships for essay winners at the chapter, state, division and national levels (amounts not stated on the official page)
deadline: Not stated on the official page; set by local DAR chapters
apply: Your school selects one senior as its DAR Good Citizen; that student may then enter the scholarship contest with a personal statement and an essay. Ask your school counselor or a local DAR chapter.
eligibility: High school seniors chosen by teachers and peers for dependability, service, leadership and patriotism. One student per school per year. U.S. citizenship is not required.
notes: Award amounts and current-cycle dates are not posted on the national page.

name: Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision
value: First prize (4 teams): per student, a $10,000 Series EE savings bond at maturity, $5,000 cash, or $5,000 to a 529 plan. Second prize (4 teams): $5,000 bond, $2,500 cash, or $2,500 to a 529 plan. Finalists get a Washington, DC trip.
deadline: Coach submits the project online by 8:00 PM ET, January 27, 2027
apply: Form a team of 2 to 4 students with a teacher or coach, who registers and submits the project (abstract, description up to 11 pages, bibliography, technology launch flyer).
eligibility: U.S. or Canadian citizens living in the U.S., Canada, U.S. territories or a DoWEA school abroad, enrolled full time, age 21 or younger. High school level is grades 10 to 12.
notes: Team entry only. AI use must follow the ExploraVision AI policy and be cited.

name: U.S. Stockholm Junior Water Prize
value: U.S. national winner: $10,000 scholarship and a trip to Stockholm; international winner: $15,000
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted (the 2026 state entry deadline was April 15, 2026)
apply: Submit a water-related research paper online to your state competition (regional science fair winners or self-nominated students).
eligibility: High school students in grades 9 to 12 who have done a water-related science project and are at least 15 by August 1 of the competition year; residents of the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico.
notes: The 2027 cycle has not been posted yet. Individual or two-person team projects.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) Grand Awards
value: Over $7 million in awards; category Grand Awards of $6,000, $2,400, $1,200 and $600; top awards up to $100,000 (George D. Yancopoulos Innovator Award), two $75,000 awards and several $50,000 awards
deadline: Qualify through a Society-affiliated science fair; ISEF 2027 is in Los Angeles in May 2027
apply: Compete at a Society-affiliated regional or state fair that sends finalists to Regeneron ISEF.
eligibility: High school students who advance from a Society-affiliated fair.
notes: Affiliated fair dates and rules vary by fair. Team awards are split equally.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
value: $250,000 post-secondary scholarship, plus $50,000 for a teacher and a $100,000 science lab for the school
deadline: 2026 submissions closed September 15, 2026; the next cycle is not posted
apply: Submit an original video explaining a science or math concept and review at least five other entries.
eligibility: Students ages 13 to 18. The 2026 rules required entrants to be no older than 18 (not yet 19) on October 1.
notes: Check the age limit for the next cycle before planning to enter. A popular vote is one route to the semifinals, but winners are chosen by judges.

name: Diamond Challenge
value: More than $100,000 prize pool; awards to top three teams in business and social innovation tracks plus topical prizes
deadline: Submission deadline January 14, 2027 at 5 PM EST
apply: Submit a 3 to 5 page concept narrative and a 60-second video online; advancing teams pitch live or by video.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 4 high school students aged 14 to 18 at the submission deadline, with an adult advisor aged 21 or older. Open worldwide.
notes: Finalists must attend the Limitless World Summit (April 29 to 30, 2027) in person. Prize money goes to the venture or is split among team members.

name: The Paradigm Challenge
value: Grand prize $100,000; 1st place $10,000 (2 teams); 2nd $2,000 (3 teams); 3rd $1,000 (3 teams); finalists $200
apply: Submit an idea (poster, video, invention, app, event or other) addressing the current Challenge project, individually or as a team.
eligibility: Students aged 4 to 18 as of the date the entry is submitted, anywhere in the world. Ages 14 to 18 form their own division.
notes: You must be 18 or younger when you submit.

name: Stossel in the Classroom Essay Contest
value: High school division: first $2,500, second $1,000, third $500, five finalists $200, five semifinalists $100, 15 honorable mentions $50
deadline: 11:59 PM ET, March 12, 2027
apply: Write a 500 to 1,000 word essay on one of four prompts; submit on your own or through a teacher.
eligibility: High school division is grades 9 to 12 with a U.S., Canada or U.S. military address. Entrants in the 2026-27 AI Challenge cannot also enter.
notes: AI-generated or plagiarized essays are disqualified. Finalists must do a brief remote interview (May 16 to 22, 2027).

name: National Economics Challenge
value: Cash prizes (amounts not stated on the official page)
deadline: Registration for the next cycle not yet open
apply: Compete on a local team with a teacher coach at the state level; state winners advance to national rounds.
eligibility: High school students of economics. Adam Smith division: AP, IB, honors and returning competitors; David Ricardo division for others.
notes: Prize amounts and 2027 dates are not posted yet.

name: Maureen O'Donnell Scholarship for Academic Excellence
value: Up to 15 scholarships of $2,000
deadline: Not stated on the official page; applications are mailed to eligible gold medalists
apply: Earn a gold medal on an Advanced NLE exam; an application is then mailed to you.
eligibility: High school seniors who win a gold medal on the Advanced Latin Prose, Advanced Latin Poetry, or Advanced Latin Reading Comprehension Exam.
notes: Recipients must take at least one Latin or classical Greek course each semester of their first college year.

name: National Speech & Debate Tournament scholarships
value: More than $100,000 in scholarships to student competitors
deadline: 2027 tournament details not checked; qualification runs through the season
apply: Qualify for the National Tournament through NSDA competition.
eligibility: High school speech and debate competitors who qualify for the National Tournament.
notes: The official page does not list award amounts by event or 2027 dates.

name: Army ROTC Four-Year Scholarship (High School)
value: Full tuition and fees or room and board, plus $420 per month during the school year and $1,200 per year for books
deadline: Round 1 due October 12, 2026; Round 2 due January 18, 2027; Round 3 due March 8, 2027. Applications must be started by March 4, 2027.
apply: Create an account in the Army ROTC scholarship application and contact the Recruiting Operations Officer at your intended school.
eligibility: U.S. citizens, at least 17 and under 31 in the year of commissioning, with an unweighted GPA of at least 2.50, an SAT or ACT score, and passing fitness tests.
notes: Accepting requires an eight-year service obligation (active duty, Reserve, or National Guard). You can leave after freshman year without obligation.

name: AFROTC High School Scholarship Program
value: Capped or uncapped tuition scholarships (type set at award), $900 per year for books, a monthly stipend, and an option to convert to room up to $10,000 per year
deadline: Application window July 1, 2026 through December 11, 2026
apply: Create a WINGS account, complete the application checklist, counselor certification, transcript, fitness assessment, and send SAT/ACT/CLT scores.
eligibility: Students entering college and AFROTC in 2027-28. Cumulative unweighted GPA of 3.3 or higher; SAT 1310, ACT 28, or CLT 93 (no superscores). U.S. citizen, or citizenship by the end of the first college term.
notes: Winners must pass a medical exam and fitness test and serve at least four years on active duty after commissioning.

name: NROTC Four-Year National Scholarship
value: Full tuition and mandatory fees at listed schools, $750 per year for textbooks, uniforms, and a monthly subsistence allowance of $250 to $400
deadline: 2027 application dates not found on the official pages checked
apply: Apply through the NROTC online application (see the NROTC Apply Now page).
eligibility: U.S. citizens (including those in the process of naturalizing), at least 17 and not yet 23 by September 1 of the year starting college. Navy and Marine Corps options.
notes: Navy recipients serve at least five years on active duty; Marine option at least four. Confirm current deadlines with NROTC.

name: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
value: $5,000 renewable for up to four years ($20,000 total) in the most recent cycle
deadline: Next cycle not posted; the page says to apply next fall
apply: Apply online when the next cycle opens.
eligibility: High school seniors in the 50 states, DC or Puerto Rico enrolling full time at an accredited two- or four-year U.S. college, with at least a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale.
notes: The page says the program aspires to reach students in need; check whether financial need is part of selection when the application opens.

name: National Beta Scholarship
deadline: Opens November 2, 2026; due 11:59 PM EST, January 14, 2027
apply: Apply online with your National Beta ID; upload transcript and ACT/SAT scores. Top 100 semifinalists submit more material by March 14, 2027.
eligibility: Active 12th-grade Senior Beta members.
notes: Membership in a National Beta Club chapter is required.

name: Bennington Young Writers Awards
value: Per category: first $2,000, second $1,000, third $500; distinguished $250. Winners who enroll at Bennington get tuition scholarships.
deadline: Submissions accepted September 1 through November 1 at 11:59 PM ET
apply: Submit poetry, fiction, or nonfiction (1,500 words max) approved by a sponsor teacher. Grade 12 students submit through Bennington's free, non-binding application.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 to 12 worldwide. Graduates are not eligible.
notes: Free to enter. Seniors must start a Bennington application to enter.

provider: National Endowment for the Arts / Poetry Foundation / Mid Atlantic Arts
name: Poetry Out Loud
value: National champion $20,000; 2nd $10,000; 3rd $5,000; 4th to 9th $1,000; state champions $200
deadline: School and state contest dates vary; state champion registration due March 10, 2027; National Finals April 26 to 28, 2027
apply: Compete at your school or a registered local organization, then advance to regional or state finals.
eligibility: Currently enrolled students in grades 9 to 12 at schools or organizations registered with the state coordinator.
notes: Poems must come from the official 2026-27 anthology.

name: National FFA Scholarships
value: Multiple sponsor scholarships through one application (amounts vary)
deadline: 2026-27 cycle not posted (the 2025-26 member application closed January 15)
apply: Submit one National FFA scholarship application to be considered for multiple scholarships.
eligibility: Senior FFA members in high school and FFA alumni in college.
notes: Criteria vary by sponsor scholarship.

name: AAN Neuroscience Research Prize
value: $1,000 prize for each of three winners, plus travel to present at the 2027 AAN Annual Meeting; one $1,000 Bhuwan Garg prize
deadline: Applications close October 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM CT
apply: Apply online with an original neuroscience research project and write-up.
eligibility: Students enrolled in and attending grades 9 to 12 in the United States, regardless of age. Individual projects only.

provider: National Center for Women & Information Technology
name: NCWIT Aspirations in Computing High School Award
value: National and Regional Affiliate awards (Winner, Honorable Mention, Rising Star); prize details by designation are on the official page
deadline: 10:00 PM ET, October 27, 2026 (educator endorsements due November 5, 2026)
apply: Join the free AiC Community, then apply online.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 to 12 involved in technology at schools in the U.S. and territories. National awards require U.S. citizenship, permanent residency, or meeting the substantial presence test.
notes: Selected on computing aptitude, activities, leadership, persistence and plans.

name: SWE Emerging First Year Scholars
value: Multiple scholarships (SWE awarded nearly $1.6 million across all programs in 2025)
deadline: Application typically opens in February and closes in March; 2027-28 dates not posted
apply: Submit one SWE application to be considered for all Society-selected scholarships you qualify for.
eligibility: Students entering their first year of college, including high school seniors, enrolling in an ABET-accredited engineering, engineering technology, or computer science program with a GPA of 3.5/4.0 or higher.
notes: Closed for 2026-27; an interest form is open for 2027-28.

name: Ron Brown Scholarship
value: $40,000 ($10,000 per year for four years); 20 awarded annually
deadline: Application due December 1; transcripts and recommendations due December 15
apply: Apply through the Ron Brown online portal.
eligibility: Black/African American current high school seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
notes: Financial need is a factor in selection, along with academics, leadership, writing and service.

name: HSF Scholar Program
value: $500 to $5,000 depending on available funds and relative need, plus scholar support services
deadline: 2027 application not yet posted
apply: Apply online and submit the FAFSA.
eligibility: Students of Hispanic heritage who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or DACA; high school students need at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale; plan to enroll full time at an accredited public or nonprofit four-year U.S. college.
notes: Scholars are selected on merit, but award amounts are based on relative need.

name: JEA Journalist of the Year Scholarship
value: $4,000 for the national winner; $1,200 each for up to five finalists
deadline: State deadlines vary; state winners' national applications were due March 15 in the last cycle (2027 date not posted)
apply: Submit a portfolio to your state JEA Journalist of the Year contest; state winners complete the national application.
eligibility: High school seniors whose portfolio wins their state JOY contest.
notes: National application needs a transcript, three recommendations, a resume, a personal narrative and an online portfolio.

name: Access/VSA Emerging Young Artists Program
value: $3,000 stipend for each of 15 artists, plus professional development and an exhibition
deadline: Apply by November 19 for the 2027 program
apply: Submit artwork through the Creative West CaFE opportunities portal.
eligibility: Artists with disabilities, ages 16 to 25, residing in the United States.
notes: The 2027 theme is Thrive.

name: International Thespian Society Senior Scholarships
value: $1,000 to $1,500 each (Board of Directors, Presidents' Leadership, Michael J. Peitz Leadership, Christopher L. Hunt, Future Theatre Educator, and other named awards)
deadline: Application period January 1 to April 1
apply: Apply online during the application period.
eligibility: Inducted Thespians who are graduating seniors; each named award has its own criteria (for example leadership, theatre education major, or business and marketing plans).
notes: Some awards are limited to specific student backgrounds or majors.

name: JRF Scholarship
value: Multi-year college scholarship plus mentoring, internships and support services (amount not stated on the application page)
deadline: Application, recommendation and CSS Profile due 5:00 PM EST, January 14, 2027
apply: Apply online with one recommendation, transcript, SAT or ACT score, activities, household information, CSS Profile and three short essays.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors who are U.S. citizens with academic excellence, leadership and community service, and evidence of financial need.
notes: Financial need is required. JRF says it is merit-based and you do not need to be an athlete.

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 per year for four years (up to $40,000) toward unmet need, plus a paid Amazon internship
deadline: 2025-26 closed; next cycle not posted
apply: Sign up on the official page to be notified when the next cycle opens.
eligibility: U.S. high school seniors who have taken a computer science course (or opt into an Amazon assessment), are authorized to work in the U.S., and plan a computer science degree.
notes: Applicants must demonstrate financial need; the award covers unmet need.

name: High School Poster Contest
value: First $1,000; second $500; third $250; up to five honorable mentions of $100
deadline: Entries must be postmarked by February 11, 2027
apply: Mail an original poster that includes the statement "You can make a difference".
eligibility: High school students in grades 9 to 12 living in the United States.
notes: Posters made with AI are not eligible.
